newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sick Indonesian labour leader returns to jail.
newsitem.headline: Sick Indonesian labour leader returns to jail.

text.p: Indonesian labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan, on trial for subversion, has returned to prison after refusing a request by doctors at a police hospital that he be admitted overnight for tests, his wife said.
"He does not want to stay overnight in Kramat Jati police hospital and has asked to be transferred to the Cikini (Christian-run) hospital," Pakpahan's wife Rosintan told Reuters.
She said a police doctor who examined her husband had suggested he stay overnight at the hospital. Pakpahan was accompanied by his wife, a family doctor and a lawyer from the Legal Aid Institute.

Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), was detained in July and charged with subversion after riots in the capital Jakarta on July 27, the worst in the capital in more than 20 years.
Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.
His lawyers have said that during an earlier prison sentence Pakpahan believed he was given poor treatment in a military-run hospital generally used for sick prisoners.

Rosintan said her husband had returned to Cipinang prison after a number of tests and would await the outcome of a meeting between the prison head and the director-general for prisons, who will decide whether Pakpahan can be admitted to a civilian hospital.
Rosintan said her husband was suffering from pain in his right hand, headaches and chest pains, adding the cause was still not clear.
The International Confederation of Free Trade Unions (ICFTU) last week expressed concern about Pakpahan's deteriorating medical condition during his detention at Cipinang.

"Following various ailments suffered earlier in prison, Brother Pakpahan now complains of a sudden deterioration which may be connected with his known heart condition," ICFTU general secretary Bill Jordan said in a letter to the justice minister last week.

Lawyers said Pakpahan's trial, which began in December, was adjourned on Monday after he complained that neither the prison head nor regional officials of the justice department would consent to him being examined by his own doctor as allowed by under the criminal procedure code.
Pakpahan was jailed in 1994 on charges that he incited racial rioting in the north Sumatran city of Medan after a series of strikes.
He was freed on appeal and his conviction was quashed by the Supreme Court, only to have the conviction reinstated in a highly unusual decision last year after his arrest on the subversion charge.
